A removed pack is not downloaded again at the next launch or on update
Both actions are keyboard accessible in Settings and covered by component tests

tickets.title: Instrument interaction latency spans and publish one p50/p95/p99 report for every MASTER section 7 and 9.11 row
tickets.summary: Only reveal (M2-0039), local Stop (M2-0081), wake-to-frame (M2-0093), Agent Home (M2-0100) and idle CPU/memory (M2-0166/0200) have budgets in acceptance. acceptance: Content-free monotonic spans for shortcut or click to first frame, speech end to partial, stable intent, prepared decision, dispatch, verified result (warm and cold), end of turn to first audible, Stop to revoked and Stop to playback flushed, plus server spans for upstream ready, stable final and worker overhead (staging worker)
A report computes p50/p95/p99, failure rate and sample count per hardware, network and language slice with failures and timeouts kept in the denominator

budgets.md is regenerated on T3, rc1 and the frozen candidate; the lane gate fails a train build on a breach unless an owner-approved exception is recorded
Shortcut to first command frame is p95 <= 150 ms on packaged macOS and Windows builds

tickets.title: Run a two-hour long-meeting soak on each platform
tickets.summary: MASTER section 9.11 and TASK-060 require a 2-hour meeting soak on each primary platform with bounded memory, ordered segment offsets and no abandoned sockets or helpers. acceptance: A 2-hour synthetic-meeting soak runs on packaged macOS and Windows builds of T3 and rc1 with the realtime speech path

Results attach to M2-0166 and M2-0210 evidence

tickets.title: Declare the advertised language scope and qualify each language separately for commands and dictation with pre-registered targets
tickets.summary: M2-0113 covers FR/EN and freezes definitions but sets no values; fixtures are en/, fr/ and mixed/ only. acceptance: The advertised language scope is recorded; unlisted languages show as unavailable or limited in the app

Permissioned synthetic fr-CA, accented-English and (if advertised) es and pt-BR sets are added to scripts/qa/asr-fixtures with manifest entries and a contract test; cloud-stt-language.ts maps each advertised language with no silent fallback
The pre-registered spec lists corpus size, speakers, slices (including noise), WER, critical-fact and no-fabrication targets before scoring; the holdout includes plausible-but-wrong glossary matches

Dictation verbatim-fidelity tests pass in every advertised language and the optional rewrite is labelled as a rewrite

tickets.title: Flag uncertain transcript words and let users correct amounts and negations with provenance that propagates to derivatives
tickets.summary: UC-034, UC-038 and master-r11-12 require uncertainty flags, provisional/provider-final/user-edited labels and user corrections kept distinct from provider output and propagated to summaries, actions and memory. acceptance: Segments carry provisional, provider-final or user-edited status; provider low-confidence words render flagged and are never auto-replaced by a glossary match; where the provider returns no confidence the UI says so
A user corrects a word, amount or negation in a segment; it is stored as a separate human revision with author and time and the provider text is kept
Summaries, action items and brain entities regenerated after a correction use and cite it; a rebuild keeps the correction; memory projection uses the corrected revision (outbox test)

tickets.title: Enforce one capture-source lease per meeting occurrence with explicit gap-aware handover
tickets.summary: EXP-07 requires one source per occurrence across desktop, bot and import, an explicit gap-aware handover, no resumption of expired recording authority after a crash or reboot, and imports that cannot arm desktop actions or bypass retention. acceptance: There is one lease per occurrence; a second source is refused or handed over explicitly with the gap marked
After a crash or reboot, expired authority does not resume capture
Imported transcripts cannot arm actions and follow the selected retention profile

tickets.title: Make the meeting bot a named, visible, silent participant with notices, Pause/Stop/Leave and a measured start-to-join goal
tickets.summary: master-r11-48/49 require joining as a named visible participant, notices that also reach late joiners, silence with the camera off and no chat, Pause, Stop and Leave, leaving on objection, actual start to first join request p95 <= 5 s and an explicit end status per meeting. acceptance: The bot joins with a configured visible name, camera off and no chat, and posts a notice that also reaches late joiners

Every occurrence ends with an explicit status

tickets.title: Structure the Intelligence briefing as changed/confirmed/uncertain/needs action with a since-last-review diff, deterministic money and time, and a usability run

acceptance: The briefing groups items into changed, confirmed, uncertain and needs action from facts computed in code, each source-linked

Fixture: the last commitment is reachable in two interactions and wrong-account, guest and expired-source cases disclose nothing; a usability session with at least five nontechnical participants on synthetic data records task success

tickets.title: Show honest synchronization states for saves and Dust writes

tickets.title: Build authenticated knowledge export and import, explicit-principal sharing and end-of-lifecycle controls
tickets.summary: EXP-11 requires round-trip exports, subset imports, CSV and HTML injection tests, redaction, wrong-audience links and expired links that reveal nothing; master-r11-66 adds that uninstall never deletes the selected external knowledge space. tickets.title: Declare one audience for the plaintext knowledge mirror and inventory its readers

tickets.title: Qualify the knowledge projection and the Graphify bridge: malicious documents, deleted sources, circular evidence, pinned Graphify and ACL-aware atomic refresh

tickets.title: Reconcile the single memory path: inventory existing call sites and decide where the gateway lives

tickets.title: Qualify the deployed Hindsight profile: /version, OpenAPI, per-bank config readback, model configuration and storage inventory

tickets.title: Port the r11 memory client and gateway tests and the reference HTTP adapter invariants into CI

tickets.title: Test every direct Hindsight route against the identity boundary (HSAC-06 route matrix)

tickets.title: Expose the application memory API with why-used and status operations, request limits and an ordered request trace

A query spanning several banks is authorized per bank, deduplicated and charged to one budget
status returns projection state per source id without content
Each memory-using request records authorize, scope, recall, source revalidation, audience recheck, release; a test fails if the order differs

tickets.title: Harden memory projection: allowed and excluded kinds, snapshot builder, event time, replace-only, per-item outcomes and no secrets
tickets.summary: M2-0134 enforces approved-before-projection and revision mapping but omits the contract policy (METIS-MEMORY-CONTRACT.example.json:30-45: excluded kinds, event time with time zone, replace-only), the snapshot builder and minimization, zero-fact detection, batch and attachment rules, per-item outcomes, polling backoff, webhook auth/dedupe, stable worker ids, stuck-operation cleanup, MASTER section 35's distinct states, and refusal while retention_days, owner or endpoint are null (contract:72-77). Snapshots are minimized to subject, speaker, canonical event time with explicit time zone and a reported/verified/inferred label; preferences are stored as kind=preference and never returned or cited as facts; updates use replace and append is rejected
States queued, upstream-accepted, indexed, recall-verified and failed are distinct; nothing shows available or learned before a recall probe returns the item

A zero-fact retain alerts and stays not-available; batches report per-item outcomes and refuse oversized attachments; webhooks are authenticated and deduplicated; polling backs off; workers have stable ids; stuck operations are reconciled and cleaned after a bound

Real-content retain refuses while retention_days, the retention owner or the endpoint is null; promoting personal memory to a team scope is a separate reviewed step and meeting recording consent never marks an item approved

tickets.title: Enforce the recall policy: one bounded call per turn, fixed envelope limits, hard date filters, negation and alias safety, local-only no-egress and canonical merge
tickets.summary: METIS-MEMORY-CONTRACT.example.json and METIS-PROFILE.md fix the initial envelope (1 recall per relevant turn, 32 candidates, 8 items, 12,000 bytes, 1,500 fact tokens, world/experience, strict non-empty tags, 8,000-character query); M2-0135 AC1 enforces only whole-envelope size. acceptance: Contract constants for calls per turn, candidates, items, envelope bytes, fact tokens, types and query length live in src/shared/contracts/memory/ with fixtures; 40 candidates, a 9th item or an oversized fact are truncated explicitly and the envelope never exceeds 12,000 UTF-8 bytes
A date-bounded question applies a hard time-interval filter after recall and before release (HMUC-024); an unavailable service returns 'unavailable', never empty
Negated statements keep their negation and aliases never merge distinct canonical people (multilingual fixtures)

The query builder sets query_timestamp and a low budget from the task, never raw transcript; an empty protected scope is rejected before egress; a scope resolving to no bank returns 'no memory' with no global fallback; in local-only mode no request reaches remote memory, embedding, rerank or reflection endpoints (egress test)
The context builder merges memory with canonical retrieval; the current source wins on conflict; with memory disabled the same question still gets a source-backed answer

tickets.title: Fence memory derivatives and bank generations on forget and permission change, with a staged deletion ledger
tickets.summary: M2-0136 covers tombstone-before-purge, backup restore and late jobs, and M2-0135 relies on flagging mental models stale, which HSAC-12 rejects. acceptance: The deletion ledger records canonical deletion, retrieval block, derivative purge, external replicas, backups/legal hold and completion as separate stages per item
Forgetting a source blocks every derived fact through lineage and epoch before purge; a delayed job or restored backup cannot return it
A permission change quarantines the affected bank generation before the next retrieval and rebuilds the permitted remainder
Two replicas projecting one document hold a scope lease; a crash after write is reconciled against actual service state and remote ETag before retry
Registry rotation and collision tests: a rotated generation never serves old data and two scopes never map to one bank

tickets.title: Sweep every memory sink with content sentinels and record the derived-store disclosure and privacy approval
tickets.summary: M2-0149 sweeps speech and follow-on routes and does not depend on any memory ticket; HM-04 is a kit_ref there and HSAC-16/17 are kit_refs on M2-0137/0133. acceptance: A synthetic sentinel retained, recalled, corrected and forgotten never appears in logs, queues, operation payloads, traces, exception reports or object stores, only in approved tables of the storage inventory (CI on the compose profile)
Memory operational logs and queues hold only ids, revisions, counts and enums (allowlist projection test)
A derived-store disclosure (what, where, retention, deletion) and the privacy owner's dated approval exist before any real-content retain; the activation gate checks both

tickets.title: Route Dust, server skills and named agents through the governed memory API

A Dust write that commits a canonical change triggers the projection outbox and a later recall returns the new revision
Named agents read only their own and explicitly shared scopes; renaming an agent keeps its identity (HMUC-005)
No Dust or skill module holds Hindsight credentials or imports the memory client (dependency rule in CI)

tickets.title: Complete the memory UX: modes, why-used, correct and inspect, distinguishable failure and removal states, agent threads and a remembered preference after restart
tickets.summary: M2-0137 requires approve/forget, per-agent isolation, ephemeral/local-only and 'historical memory unavailable'; the M2-0201 memory STATE-LIST covers review, forget, isolation, outage and local-only only (validation BLOCKED_EXTERNAL). Missing: disabled/read-only/read-write modes, why-used, source, correct and inspect (HM-13, CXSTEP-13), other failure states, 'removal still in progress' (ADR-019 section 8), source/assertion/conclusion vocabulary, agent threads resuming across restarts, a per-agent job-memory view (HC-08), and the CXAC-26 remember-then-restart proof.
acceptance: Modes disabled, read-only and read/write exist per organization and user; after disabling, a meeting plus question records zero retain and recall calls; a 403 surfaces as a denial, not an outage

Every recalled item used in an answer shows why it was used, its current source, and Correct, Inspect and Forget; correcting updates the canonical record first and invalidates the stale read; labels distinguish original source, extracted assertion and generated conclusion

Distinct states for unavailable, denied, not yet indexed, partial, revoked and 'not used anymore; removal still in progress', each unit-tested and captured; the M2-0201 STATE-LIST gains recall, correction, revocation and purge-pending, validated by an Opus session other than the author
Approve a language preference, restart, start a relevant task: recall cites the current canonical source; an unrelated command performs no recall (CXAC-26 on staging)

An agent's thread resumes across restarts with its context and drafts, isolated per agent; each agent has one dated, compact job-memory view where entries are corrected or forgotten in place; the memory area sits inside Knowledge & skills and Intelligence with no memory-specific orb

tickets.title: Enforce JEV and memory role separation: no retain, approval or verification from a decision, and a separately qualified reranker

Sign-out and membership change must also invalidate pending memory reads.
acceptance: A confident JEV decision and an Intelligence classification produce zero retain calls and no projection outbox entry
A JEV result cannot mark an action verified or satisfy an approval
Sign-out, membership change and consent withdrawal invalidate pending memory reads and queued projections for that principal

The memory reranker uses its own credential and qualification record with a pinned model, never jev-latest; configuring JEV or Laya for decisions does not enable memory reranking; Laya is never configured as an embedder (config tests)

tickets.title: Add the memory activation gate, approval records for risky actions and per-platform release claims
tickets.summary: HOST-BINDINGS section F requires version, OpenAPI, config, model, region and customer-data approval before activation; the memory contract leaves retention and endpoint null. acceptance: ACTIVATION-CHECKLIST.md lists version, OpenAPI hash, config readback, model configuration, region, retention owner and days, customer-data and privacy approval; the service stays disabled until every item is recorded
Real-data retain, live smoke, Docker deployment and billable provider calls each require a dated approval record; tests show refusal without it
The release decision (M2-0171) fails when release notes claim memory on a platform without a LIVE_VERIFIED memory proof for that platform
Release qualification records the memory service version, image digest and DB version

tickets.title: Extend the Hindsight live proof: Dust/agent readback, packaged Windows and Mac artifacts, a second device and the full fault matrix
tickets.summary: M2-0138 proofs A-H lack an authorized Dust/agent readback (HSAC-20), runs on packaged Windows, Mac and a second device (HM-16, HMUC-032), portal reconciliation and the team-memory step in the meeting-to-knowledge journey (HM-FLOW-02), and inject only outage, restart and delayed completion (HMSTEP-13, HM-FLOW-04).

Portal usage for the journey reconciles with the service ledger

The M2-0176 meeting-to-knowledge journey includes the scoped team-memory step (approve, project to team scope, teammate recall); each step maps to its HM-FLOW id in the evidence record

tickets.title: Bring the native Mac app to command-journey parity over the shared contracts and label native evidence separately

tickets.title: Inject native persistence failures and enforce summary-only storage in MetisKit
tickets.summary: SRC-11 requires typed save results, readback, telling corrupt data apart from an empty meeting, and summary-only storage on native Mac. M2-0118 AC3 makes failures visible but has no injected failure matrix or summary-only criterion.
